lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: selecting linear or nonlinear models

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: As study time increases, scores tend to increase. Identify the trend.

steps: Define the relevant quantities and assumptions.
State a conclusion with its limitation or evidence.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A line of fit was made from data for temperatures 40° through 80°. It is used to predict a temperature at 120°. Which limitation is most important?
choices: The line proves causation.
The data range no longer matters.
The prediction is an extrapolation and may be less reliable.
The prediction must be exactly correct.

items.prompt: Which action provides the strongest evidence that a model fits a situation?
choices: show calculations and compare predictions to data
state an answer without units
choose the first equation written
ignore data that disagree

items.prompt: Which conclusion communicates a mathematical model responsibly?
choices: State the result, units, assumption, and limitation.
Hide the assumption and data source.
Claim the model is always correct.
State only a number.

items.prompt: A moving company charges by the number of hours worked. Which definition of x best models this situation?
choices: x = number of hours worked
x = total cost in dollars
x = number of workers
x = company name

items.prompt: A service is modeled by C = 12h + 25, where h is hours. Which assumption supports this model?
choices: The flat fee changes each hour.
The number of hours is always zero.
The hourly charge remains $12 for every hour.
Every service has the same total cost.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: The area of a square changes as its side length is squared. Which model type is appropriate?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A model gives 12x + 17 = 41. What is x?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Two constraints are y = 1x + 0 and y = 6x - 40. What is their shared solution?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
